title: U.S. House · Wisconsin's 1st Congressional District
area: Southeastern Wisconsin, including Racine, Kenosha, and Janesville.

context.text: Incumbent Bryan Steil (R) advanced from the August 11, 2026 Republican primary unopposed. Mitchell Berman defeated Peter Burgelis, Lorenzo Santos, and Miguel Aranda in the Democratic primary. As of late September 2026, outlets tracked by Ballotpedia rated the general election Lean Republican to Likely Republican.

candidates.name: Bryan Steil
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced from the Republican primary unopposed.
candidates.currentRole: U.S. Representative for Wisconsin's 1st Congressional District (since 2019)

summary.text: Bryan Steil is the Republican incumbent for Wisconsin's 1st Congressional District, which he has represented since 2019 after succeeding Paul Ryan. A Janesville native, he worked in Wisconsin manufacturing and served on the University of Wisconsin Board of Regents before running for Congress. He chairs the House Administration Committee and sits on the Financial Services Committee, and is seeking re-election.

background.text: Born March 3, 1981, and raised in Janesville, Wisconsin; graduated from Janesville Craig High School.
Earned a bachelor's degree from Georgetown University and a law degree from the University of Wisconsin-Madison Law School.
Worked as an aide to Rep. Paul Ryan in 2003, according to Wikipedia.

Spent a decade in Wisconsin's manufacturing industry before Congress, according to his House website, first with an industrial motion control manufacturer in Beloit and later at a plastics manufacturer in Milton.
Appointed to the University of Wisconsin Board of Regents by the governor in 2016 and unanimously confirmed by the Wisconsin Senate.
Won the 2018 Republican primary for the open seat of retiring Speaker Paul Ryan and the general election that year; took office January 3, 2019.

In the 117th Congress served as Ranking Member of the Select Committee on the Economy; appointed Chairman of the Committee on House Administration in 2023, and also chairs its Subcommittee on Digital Assets, Financial Technology, and Artificial Intelligence while sitting on the Financial Services Committee.
His House website says he authored the Expanding Investment in Small Businesses Act of 2019, which passed the House 417-2 in July 2019, and the Exposing the Financing of Human Trafficking Act.
Co-chaired the Middle Class Jobs Caucus and the Future of Work Caucus; his House website lists him as a member of St. John Vianney Parish in Janesville.

priorities.text: Says Congress needs to restore fiscal responsibility and find common ground on the national debt.
priorities.quote: Congress needs a healthy dose of Wisconsin commonsense. Families in our state know how to balance their checkbooks, and it's time Congress does the same.

priorities.text: Says over-regulation and federal red tape hinder innovation and job growth, and supports keeping government "hands off" small businesses.
Says education decisions are best made locally and wants more transparency for parents in their children's education.

positions.summary: Says defunding the police is a dangerous idea and that he supports law enforcement.
positions.quote: Defunding the police is a dangerous idea that will make our communities less safe. We must support our men and women of law enforcement.

positions.summary: Emphasizes fiscal responsibility, reducing the national debt, and reducing tax and regulatory burdens rather than raising taxes.
Says Washington bureaucrats and the federal government should not dictate individual health care needs, and favors putting patients and doctors at the center of decisions.

record.text: Chairs the Committee on House Administration and the Joint Committee on the Library; also serves on the Committee on Financial Services in the 119th Congress.
Co-chairs the Congressional Future of Work Caucus.

candidates.name: Mitchell Berman
candidates.ballotNote: Defeated Peter Burgelis, Lorenzo Santos, and Miguel Aranda in the Democratic primary.

summary.text: Mitchell Berman is the Democratic nominee for Wisconsin's 1st Congressional District and a first-time candidate. A registered nurse with more than two decades of healthcare experience, he spent a decade at a Department of Veterans Affairs hospital. He describes himself as running on lowering costs, health care, and ending corruption in Washington.

background.text: According to his campaign website, raised in a one-stoplight rural Wisconsin town, the son of a small roofing business owner and a foundry worker, and a product of Wisconsin public schools.
Describes himself as the first in his family to graduate from college, earning his degree while working three jobs and taking out student loans; got his nursing assistant license at 17.

Registered nurse with more than 23 years of healthcare experience, including more than a decade at the Department of Veterans Affairs serving veterans and active-duty servicemembers; remains a board-certified emergency nurse, according to his campaign website. The Wisconsin Examiner describes him as an emergency room nurse.
Has been a union member since his first union job with Teamsters Local 344 in college, later with the Wisconsin Federation of Nurses and Health Professionals and National Nurses United.
First-time candidate, aged 40 per the Associated Press; says cuts to the VA affecting the VA hospital where he worked as a nurse motivated his run.

Won the August 11, 2026 Democratic primary with 44.1% of the vote over Peter Burgelis, Lorenzo Santos, and Miguel Aranda; his campaign lists endorsements including the United Auto Workers, and the Wisconsin Examiner reports UAW and several state legislators backed him.
His campaign website describes him as a husband and father of two girls; the campaign lists a Racine mailing address.

priorities.text: Says he will fight to lower costs for working families.
Says he will fight to protect the healthcare Wisconsinites depend on.
Says he will safeguard programs that feed Wisconsin kids and stop what he calls giveaways to corporations and billionaires.

positions.summary: Campaign says he will fight to protect the healthcare Wisconsinites depend on, drawing on his career as a nurse who has seen patients fear losing coverage.
Campaign says he will fight to stop what he describes as giveaways to corporations and billionaires.

candidates.researchNotes: No public voting or legislative record exists; Berman has not held elected office. He has not completed Ballotpedia's Candidate Connection survey.
